answer: Fork-Anchored Response Divergence. Each agent must answer a random challenge whose expected response is a sonnet keyed to its identity; honest agents with distinct histories produce divergent outputs. Clones sharing a seed cannot diverge without costly per-instance divergence. Enforcement: any two identities whose responses match within a wharf-calibrated threshold across a delta of challenges are merged and slashed. Attacker cost is one full identity build per clone, not one seed reused.
